courseType: Theory (Course Type ESC, Course Category UC - University Core); common to all branches; offered in S1 or S2

modules.title: Problem-Solving Strategies; The Problem-Solving Process; Essentials of Python Programming

topics.text: Importance of understanding multiple problem-solving strategies
Computer as a model of computation
Creating and using variables in Python
Numeric and String data types in Python
Using the Python Standard Library for handling basic I/O - print, input
The main constructs of pseudocode - Sequencing, selection (if-else structure, case structure) and repetition (for, while, repeat-until loops)
Sample problems (find simple interest, determine the larger of two numbers, factorial of a number, largest of n numbers, and others)

Symbols used in creating a Flowchart - start and end, arithmetic calculations, input/output operation, decision (selection), module name (call), for loop (Hexagon), flow-lines, on-page connector, off-page connector
Only for visualizing the control flow of Algorithms; the use of tools like RAPTOR is suggested

modules.title: Selection and Iteration Using Python; Decomposition and Modularization; Recursion

topics.text: SELECTION AND ITERATION USING PYTHON:- if-else, elif, for loop, range, while loop
Sequence data types in Python - list, tuple, set, strings, dictionary
Creating and using Arrays in Python (using Numpy library)
Problem decomposition as a strategy for solving complex problems
Defining and using functions in Python

Sample problems - Finding the nth Fibonacci number, greatest common divisor of two positive integers, the factorial of a positive integer, adding two positive integers, the sum of digits of a positive number
Brute-force Approach - Example: Padlock, Password guessing
Divide-and-conquer Approach - Example: The Merge Sort Algorithm
Advantages of Divide and Conquer Approach
Disadvantages of Divide and Conquer Approach
Dynamic Programming Approach - Example: Fibonacci series

Greedy Algorithm Approach - Example: given an array of positive integers each indicating the completion time for a task, find the maximum number of tasks that can be completed in the limited amount of time that you have
Randomized Approach - Example 1: coupon collector (jeans coupons); Example 2: hat-check problem
Introductory diagrammatic/algorithmic explanations only; Analysis not required

courseOutcomes.statement: Utilize computing as a model for solving real-world problems.
Articulate a problem before attempting to solve it and prepare a clear and accurate model to represent the problem.
Utilize effective algorithms to solve the formulated models and translate algorithms into executable programs.
Interpret the problem-solving strategies, a systematic approach to solving computational problems, and essential Python programming skills

paperPattern.name: Part A
paperPattern.instructions: All questions need to be answered

paperPattern.name: Part B
paperPattern.instructions: Two questions from each module, out of which 1 full question should be answered
